content.value_statement: Startup teams need credible projections before planning hiring, fundraising, and cash use. This skill guides structured models for revenue, costs, runway, and scenarios.
actual_capabilities: Guides 3-5 year financial model structure with monthly and quarterly projection horizons.
Builds cohort-based revenue projections for SaaS, marketplace, e-commerce, and services models.
Defines cost structure, headcount plan, cash flow, burn rate, and runway calculations.
Creates conservative, base, and optimistic scenarios using variable assumptions.
Calculates startup metrics such as CAC, LTV, burn multiple, gross margin, and dilution.
limitations: Does not include executable spreadsheets, scripts, or calculators.
Uses benchmark ranges, so users must supply company-specific assumptions.
Does not replace accounting, tax, legal, or investment advice.
References additional files that are not present in this audited package.

use_cases.title: Plan Fundraising Runway
use_cases.description: Estimate cash needs, burn rate, milestones, and funding timing before investor conversations.

use_cases.title: Prepare Board Forecasts
use_cases.description: Create base, conservative, and optimistic projections for revenue, expenses, hiring, and cash.

use_cases.title: Compare Business Models
use_cases.description: Model SaaS, marketplace, e-commerce, or services revenue drivers before choosing a strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Runway Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 24-month runway model for my startup. Ask for current cash, monthly revenue, fixed costs, variable costs, and planned hires.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Cohort Revenue Forecast
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a three-year SaaS revenue forecast using cohorts. Include new customers, ARPU, retention, expansion revenue, churn, MRR, and ARR.

prompt_templates.title: Model Three Operating Scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Create conservative, base, and optimistic scenarios for our startup. Vary acquisition, churn, CAC, hiring timing, and average contract value.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Fundraising Dilution
prompt_templates.prompt: Model a funding round for our startup. Include pre-money valuation, investment amount, dilution, use of funds, runway, and milestone coverage.

output_examples.input: A pre-seed SaaS company has $600,000 cash, $25,000 MRR, and $85,000 monthly expenses.
output_examples.output: The model estimates net burn, runway, ARR growth, hiring capacity, and funding timing under three operating scenarios.

output_examples.input: A marketplace wants projections for GMV, take rate, buyer growth, seller growth, and contribution margin.
output_examples.output: The output separates gross merchandise value from net revenue and highlights take-rate sensitivity, CAC pressure, and cash needs.

output_examples.input: A founder wants to raise $4 million at a $16 million pre-money valuation.
output_examples.output: The analysis shows post-money valuation, dilution, use of funds, expected runway extension, and milestones the round should support.

best_practices: Use separate assumptions for acquisition, retention, pricing, costs, hiring, and cash timing.
Maintain conservative, base, and optimistic scenarios for every important planning decision.
Validate outputs against unit economics, gross margin, burn multiple, and comparable company benchmarks.
anti_patterns: Do not use one aggressive revenue case as the only operating plan.
Do not ignore payment timing when calculating cash runway.
Do not treat benchmark ratios as facts without checking your business model.

faq.question: What business models does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports SaaS, marketplace, e-commerce, services, and other startup models with clear revenue drivers.

faq.question: Can it create a spreadsheet file?
faq.answer: No. It provides model structure, formulas, assumptions, and planning guidance, but this package has no spreadsheet generator.

faq.question: Does it handle fundraising scenarios?
faq.answer: Yes. It can model investment amount, valuation, dilution, use of funds, runway, and milestone coverage.

faq.question: How detailed can the forecast be?
faq.answer: The guidance supports monthly detail for early years and higher-level projections for later years.

faq.question: What inputs should I prepare?
faq.answer: Prepare cash balance, revenue, pricing, customer counts, churn, expenses, headcount, CAC, and fundraising assumptions.

faq.question: Is this financial advice?
faq.answer: No. It is planning guidance and should be reviewed with finance, accounting, legal, or investment professionals.
